venue.name: West Coast Aquatic Safaris
venue.description: West Coast Aquatic Safaris runs wildlife boat tours out of an office at 101A Fourth Street in Tofino, where guests check in before walking to the harbour. Two vessels carry the tours: WASCO, a 12 passenger cruiser, and NANUQ, a 37 passenger catamaran, both with heated indoor cabins, outdoor viewing decks and a restroom on board. The published tours are whale watching, bear watching, Hot Springs Cove, bird watching, cultural tours and private charters, and the charter page lists school functions and educational tours among the occasions it takes. NANUQ has a boarding ramp, and the office has a ramp and priority accessible parking at the harbour.
venue.address: 101A Fourth Street, PO Box 967, Tofino, BC V0R 2Z0

facility_notes.washrooms: Yes, all boats are equipped with a restroom - sink and toilet. However, we encourage guests to use our office restroom prior to departure and/or returning from the tour.
facility_notes.rain_backup: It is the "wet coast" - so we go out. WCAS provides rain jackets to use while touring and the boat has inside seating for all.
facility_notes.stroller_accessible: For safety reasons, we cannot allow strollers on our vessels, but you are welcome to leave them in our offices during your trip. For infants we recommend baby sling and carriers.
facility_notes.wheelchair_accessible: West Coast Aquatic Safaris has a ramp to provide access to the office. We also have a ramp to load aboard NANUQ, priority accessible parking at the harbour and a pre-loading protocol.
facility_notes.bus_parking: Parking ia available along Fourth St. or there is a pay parking lot on the corner of Third & Main.

restrictions: Please check in at the West Coast Aquatic Safaris office (located at 101 Fourth Street, Tofino) at least 30 minutes prior to the scheduled departure time of your tour.
All guests are required to sign a participation waiver prior to the tour departure. Guests under 18 years of age must have a guardian sign for them.
For safety reasons, we cannot allow strollers on our vessels, but you are welcome to leave them in our offices during your trip.
Any of the open water trips may not be suitable for guests who are pregnant, who have back or neck injuries, or have concerns with open ocean conditions including potential bumps during the voyage.

Dogs must have a medical note from a physician or doctor or qualified medical practitioner, as well as wear appropriate identification (harness or vest). This policy does not include therapy or emotional support dogs.
You will not be able to touch as per Canadian law.
venue.seasonal_notes: Seasons published per tour: bear watching April 1 to October 31, bird watching March 1 to October 31, Hot Springs Cove late February to late November. The whale watching page gives two different seasons for itself.

programs.name: Whale watching tour
programs.description: A guided boat tour from Tofino Harbour into Clayoquot Sound, listed at 2.5 to 3 hours with multiple daily departures. The boats are covered and heated with inside seating for all, outdoor viewing decks and a restroom on board, and the tour can be run as an accessible tour on NANUQ if you say so when booking. The site carries a whale sighting guarantee: guests who do not sight whales are invited back for another whale watching tour free of charge. The only price anywhere on the site is a CAD 159.00 figure in the page's structured data, with no child rate and no group rate stated.
programs.what_children_do: Check in at the orange office on Fourth Street, sign the waiver and hear a short safety briefing, then walk to the harbour and board. On the water they sit in a heated cabin with large windows or stand at the rail on the open decks, watching for grey whales, humpbacks, orcas, sea otters, sea lions, seals and eagles while the crew talks about what is passing. There is a toilet on board and rain jackets if the weather turns.
programs.our_note: Everyone has to be at the office half an hour before the boat leaves, and a guardian has to sign the waiver for every child under 18, so build that into the morning. Strollers cannot go aboard, though the office will hold them, and they suggest a sling or carrier for babies. Nothing on the site sets a youngest age, so ask whether two and a half hours afloat suits your group.
programs.practical_summary: There are washrooms in the office and on every boat, the cabin is heated and covered, and tours run rain or shine. No child price, no youngest age and no group rate are published, and nothing is said about bus parking or anywhere to eat, so it is worth a call.
programs.payment_timing: Tour bookings are not confirmed or guaranteed until payment is processed.
programs.cancellation_note: 48 hour notice is required on all cancellations or changes. Inside 48 hours there is no cash refund and no date change, but they issue a rain check voucher or a credit that can be used on a standby basis and does not expire.

programs.name: Bear watching tour
programs.description: A guided boat tour listed at 2 to 2.5 hours, departing daily at low tide from Tofino Harbour and running April 1 to October 31. The route stays in sheltered inside passages by Meares Island, Fortune Channel or Tofino Inlet, which their booking policy page points to as the gentler option for anyone worried about a bumpy ride. Boats are covered and heated with a restroom on board, and the tour can be run as an accessible tour on request. The only price on the site is a CAD 159.00 figure in the page's structured data, with no child or group rate stated.
programs.what_children_do: Board at Tofino Harbour and ride about 30 minutes through calm sheltered water past Meares Island, Fortune Channel or Tofino Inlet. The boat then works slowly along the shoreline at low tide while the children watch coastal black bears turn over rocks and boulders looking for crab and clams, with bald eagles, sea lions, seals, porpoises and occasionally wolves along the way.
programs.our_note: This is the sheltered one, so it suits a group you would rather not take onto open ocean. Departures follow the low tide rather than a fixed timetable, which means the start time moves from day to day, so confirm it before you book a bus or set a pickup. It is also the shortest of their wildlife tours at around two hours.
programs.practical_summary: Heated covered boat with a toilet aboard, washrooms at the office, and rain does not cancel it. The youngest age, any child price, any group rate, bus parking and anywhere to eat are all unpublished.
programs.payment_timing: Tour bookings are not confirmed or guaranteed until payment is processed.
programs.cancellation_note: 48 hour notice is required on all cancellations or changes. Inside 48 hours there is no cash refund and no date change, but they issue a rain check voucher or a credit that can be used on a standby basis and does not expire.

programs.name: Hot Springs Cove excursion
programs.description: A full day trip to Nismaakqin Park, formerly Maquinna Provincial Park, listed on the questions page at 6 hours. It is a 90 minute covered and heated boat ride north from Tofino Harbour, then a 2 km cedar boardwalk with stairs and uneven surfaces that takes 35 to 40 minutes each way, then up to three hours at the park to soak in the natural thermal rock pools. The site says guests must be able to walk uneven terrain and that the trip is not stroller or wheelchair accessible, and that guests bring their own lunch, snacks and water. Small group tours are listed at a maximum of 12. No price is published.
programs.what_children_do: Ride 90 minutes up the coast from Tofino Harbour, watching for sea otters, sea lions, whales and bald eagles from the cabin or the deck. At the other end they walk a 2 km cedar boardwalk through rainforest, with stairs and uneven sections, out to the edge of the coast. There they can soak in a chain of natural hot rock pools that spill down toward the ocean, with up to three hours at the park before the boat ride home.
programs.our_note: This is a six hour day with a 2 km walk at each end, and their own page says it is not stroller or wheelchair friendly and that guests have to manage uneven ground. Everyone carries their own lunch, water and swim things. For a preschool group that is a long day on a boardwalk, so talk it through before you commit.
programs.practical_summary: There is a toilet on the boat, and change stalls, a gazebo and park washrooms at the springs. No price, youngest age, group rate or bus parking is published, and the walk rules out strollers, so a call is worth it.
programs.payment_timing: Tour bookings are not confirmed or guaranteed until payment is processed.
programs.cancellation_note: 48 hour notice is required on all cancellations or changes. Inside 48 hours there is no cash refund and no date change, but they issue a rain check voucher or a credit that can be used on a standby basis and does not expire.
programs.evidence: Small group tours (max 12) for a more personal experience

programs.name: Private charter
programs.description: A whole vessel booked privately for one group. The page lists school functions and educational tours among the things it is used for, alongside private wildlife tours, photography tours, weddings, corporate functions, birthday parties and fundraisers. The charter includes private use of a heated cabin vessel with an on board restroom and a certified marine crew, and staff say they will work with you to arrange it. The page gives the length as customise to suit, and it gives both year round departures and tour dates of April 1 to October 31 without reconciling them. No price, group size or booking lead time is published.
programs.our_note: This is the page to start from for a group, because it is the only place on the site that mentions school functions and educational tours. Nothing about it is priced, sized or scheduled, so the whole thing is a phone call. Ask which boat you would get, since one takes 12 passengers and the other takes 37.
programs.practical_summary: A private boat with a heated cabin and a restroom aboard, plus washrooms at the office before you leave. Price, group size, how far ahead to book, bus parking and any youngest age are all unpublished.
programs.payment_timing: Tour bookings are not confirmed or guaranteed until payment is processed.
programs.cancellation_note: 48 hour notice is required on all cancellations or changes. Inside 48 hours there is no cash refund and no date change, but they issue a rain check voucher or a credit that can be used on a standby basis and does not expire.

programs.name: Bird watching tour
programs.description: A three hour boat tour of Tofino and Clayoquot Sound, listed with tour dates of March 1 to October 31. The page lists bald eagles, great blue herons, osprey, tufted puffins, Steller's jays, rufous hummingbirds, western sandpipers, lesser yellowlegs, black oystercatchers, Pacific loons and pelagic cormorants among the species seen. It can be run as an accessible tour on request. No price, age guidance or group size is published.
programs.what_children_do: Ride out from Tofino for about three hours past ocean, mudflats, rocky shorelines and old growth rainforest, watching from the cabin windows and the open deck for bald eagles, herons, puffins, oystercatchers and sandpipers.
programs.our_note: The site gives this tour a length and a season and almost nothing else. There is no price, no youngest age and no word on how a group books it. Three hours is the longest of their wildlife tours apart from the hot springs day, so weigh that against a bear trip of two.
programs.practical_summary: The same boats as the other tours, so a toilet on board and washrooms at the office. Price, youngest age, group size and bus parking are not published.
programs.payment_timing: Tour bookings are not confirmed or guaranteed until payment is processed.
programs.cancellation_note: 48 hour notice is required on all cancellations or changes. Inside 48 hours there is no cash refund and no date change, but they issue a rain check voucher or a credit that can be used on a standby basis and does not expire.

programs.name: Cultural tour
programs.description: A boat tour into the ancestral territory of the Nuu-chah-nulth First Nations around Tofino and Clayoquot Sound, given as 2.5 hours on the questions page. The page names the five local tribes of the Nuu-chah-nulth tribal council, Ahousaht, Hesquiaht, Tla-o-qui-aht, Toquaht and Ucluelet, and the village of Opitsaht on Meares Island, thought to be over 5,000 years old. No price, season, age guidance or group size is published, and the page does not say who leads the storytelling.
programs.what_children_do: Travel by boat from Tofino into Nuu-chah-nulth traditional territory in Clayoquot Sound, past Meares Island and the village of Opitsaht, while the crew tells the history and traditional way of life of the five local tribes.
programs.our_note: The site gives no price, no season and no age guidance for this one. Ask who leads the storytelling and whether it is run together with the local First Nations, because the page does not say and that is worth knowing before you describe it to families.
programs.practical_summary: The same boats as the wildlife tours, with a toilet on board and washrooms at the office. Price, youngest age, season and group size are not published.
programs.payment_timing: Tour bookings are not confirmed or guaranteed until payment is processed.
programs.cancellation_note: 48 hour notice is required on all cancellations or changes. Inside 48 hours there is no cash refund and no date change, but they issue a rain check voucher or a credit that can be used on a standby basis and does not expire.
programs.evidence: Our Tofino cultural tours visit the traditional territories of the Nuu-chah-nulth while storytelling about their rich history and traditional way of life.

gaps: no minimum age is published for any tour or for either vessel; the site says only "Yes, people of all ages are welcome to tour aboard" and "Great for kids and adults of all ages", so the age range on every program is null
no weight limit and no height rule is published anywhere; life jackets are mentioned only in a customer review, not in the site's own copy

no child price is published for any tour; the only price on the site is a CAD 159.00 figure that appears in the machine readable structured data on the whale watching and bear watching pages and nowhere in the visible text. It is recorded as the adult price because it is a single unqualified per person figure with no child rate stated
no price at all is published for the Hot Springs Cove, private charter, bird watching or cultural tours
no group rate, school rate or daycare rate is published anywhere on the site
no per booking capacity is published for a group; the questions page gives vessel capacities only, WASCO at 12 passengers and NANUQ at 37
no booking lead time or minimum notice is published; the site says only that reservations are recommended for all departures
no chaperone ratio or adult to child ratio is published
no indoor lunch space is offered; the site says it does not serve lunch and encourages guests to eat after the tour, and suggests a packed lunch for the Hot Springs Cove trip
bus parking is not addressed; the directions mention street parking on Fourth Street and a pay lot at Third and Main

the site does not mention daycares, preschools or early years groups at all, so whether it hosts daycare groups is left unanswered. School functions and educational tours are named only on the private charter page

months are unknown for the private charter and the cultural tour; the charter card gives both year round departures and tour dates of April 1 to October 31, and the cultural tour page gives no season at all
months are unknown for whale watching; the tour page carries two different seasons for itself and they are recorded as a conflict
tour prices, departure times and any child rates live in an off domain booking system at whalesafaris.app.resmarksystems.com, which does not render without JavaScript, so nothing was taken from it
a second office phone number, 250-725-3330, appears in the structured data on the tour pages while every visible page gives 250-725-9227. The visible number is recorded
the whale sighting guarantee is described as a free return tour rather than a refund, which may not help a group that travels once

values: Beginning of March - End of October
conflicts.note: Their site gives two different end dates for the whale watching season. One says it runs to November, another says it ends in October. If you are looking at late October or November, check that they are still sailing before you plan the day.

Their site gives two different sets of office opening hours. One says 9am to 5pm, the other 7am to 9pm. Since everyone has to check in half an hour before the boat leaves, it is worth confirming the office is open when you plan to arrive.
Two of their pages give the street number slightly differently, 101 and 101A Fourth Street. It is the same bright orange building on Fourth Street, so either one will get your driver there.

values: Whale Watch 2.5 hours and Bear Watch 2 hours
whale 2.5 to 3 hours and bear 2 to 2.5 hours
